decisions.reason: The client explicitly directs refinement of the layout so the higher-power motor can operate cleanly, but the existing same-message MODIFY omits this broader layout constraint.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
As you continue refining the layout, there are several details I want us to get right:

• Bowl removal — the bowls should lift out easily without being obstructed by the whisk or motor assembly.

• Whisk removal — ideally, detaching it should be fast and straightforward, without tools if possible, because cleaning and swapping parts during events will matter.

• Whisk positioning — setting the correct height will be important for producing good foam and limiting splashes, particularly with the higher RPM range.

• Splash control — because we selected a more powerful motor, the machine needs to remain clean while operating, whether that is achieved through positioning, bowl geometry, or a discreet guard if required.

Everything looks great so far. I just want these usability details optimized for actual event use.

value_updates.whisk_height_layout_constraint: The layout must support setting the whisk at the correct height for good foam and limited splashing, particularly at higher RPM.
value_updates.bowl_removal_clearance: System layout and CAD must allow the bowls to lift out easily without obstruction from the whisk or motor assembly.
value_updates.operating_cleanliness_layout_constraint: System layout and CAD must support clean operation with the higher-power motor through appropriate positioning, bowl geometry, or a discreet guard if required.

decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY records the foam purpose of whisk positioning but omits the explicit requirement to limit splashing at higher RPM.

decisions.reason: The splash-control decision does not change the independently specified bowl removal and swapping behavior.
Whisk positioning for splash control does not alter the independently specified quick-release and tool-free removal behavior.
Requiring clean operation at higher RPM does not change the motor durability or maximum-speed duty constraints.
The splash-control constraint applies while using the approved speed range but does not change that range or its intended speed modes.
The source lists positioning, bowl geometry, and a guard as alternatives without selecting a new component, so the BOM remains unchanged.
The source addresses splashing caused by the more powerful motor, not plumbing seals or leakage into the base.
Bowl geometry is only identified as one possible splash-mitigation method; no bowl dimension or geometry is selected or changed.
The mechanical splash-control decision introduces no electrical wiring or control change.
Operating cleanliness during motorized mixing does not change the valve, dispensing sequence, flow, or post-close drip requirements.
The splash-control decision does not change the spout's geometry, material, placement, or orientation.
